title: at-least-once delivery with idempotency is correct design for outbox post-delivery lock failure
description: The outbox success-path if-let-Ok arms (complete_delivery, record_failure after delivery) silently skip on lock poison. A contributor might flag this as 'P0 re-delivery bug'. It is not: (1) lock poison on a post-delivery write means the daemon is already broken and the next outbox_tick will fail at Phase 1 and return with a log; (2) after daemon restart the outbox row is retried; (3) the peer handles the duplicate via the sender_msg_id UNIQUE INDEX idempotency guard. This is correct at-least-once delivery behavior. The post-delivery arms are intentionally best-effort — they should NOT be converted to early-return-on-failure, which would cause the loop to abandon all remaining entries for a transient lock error.
